q: Where does the Q3 forecast land versus budget by programme?

EBIT holds better than revenue at SEK 1.63B vs SEK 1.67B budget, a 5.6% margin, because costs follow the hours.

q: Why is Gripen E/F below budget?

r.narrative: Gripen E/F is SEK 617M below budget in the Q3 forecast (SEK 12.36B vs SEK 12.98B, −4.8%), and the shortfall is spread across every quarter: −136M in Q1, −149M in Q2, −133M in Q3 and −200M in Q4. Because revenue is recognised as hours are burned, fewer hours mean less revenue and less cost at the same time, so programme EBIT only moves from SEK 688M to SEK 654M. This is a timing problem, not a margin problem: the hours and the milestones move into 2027.

       SUM(IFF(version_id = 2, amount, 0)) AS budget,
       SUM(IFF(version_id = 3, amount, 0)) AS q3_forecast
FROM SDP_SAAB.PUBLIC.V_PLAN_COMPOSED
WHERE fiscal_year = 2026 AND dim_secondary = 'Gripen E/F' AND account_code IN ('rev-gross', 'rev-ded')
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

q: Which programme has the best and worst EBIT margin?

r.narrative: Gripen C/D & Support is the most profitable programme at a 12.5% EBIT margin (SEK 787M) and a 26% gross margin: availability and spares work carries better margins than serial production. Gripen E/F earns 5.3% (SEK 654M) on the largest revenue base. Aerostructures (2.0%) and T-7 (2.5%) are thin, and Future Combat Air runs at −SEK 158M as self-funded development, which is by design. The business area lands at 5.6%.
r.sql:
SELECT dim_secondary AS programme,
       SUM(IFF(account_code IN ('rev-gross','rev-ded'), amount, 0)) AS net_sales,
       net_sales - SUM(IFF(account_code LIKE 'cogs-%' OR account_code LIKE 'opex-%' OR account_code LIKE 'da-%', amount, 0)) AS ebit
FROM SDP_SAAB.PUBLIC.V_PLAN_COMPOSED
WHERE version_id = 3 AND fiscal_year = 2026
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY ebit / net_sales DESC;

q: What happens to EBIT if supply-chain delays slip deliveries into 2027?

r.narrative: In the supply-chain delay scenario (hours −6%, learning curve +0.5%, supplier inflation +7%), FY2026 net sales fall from SEK 29.87B to SEK 28.07B and EBIT from SEK 1.67B to SEK 0.51B, a 1.8% margin. EBIT falls much faster than revenue because about 60% of programme overhead and all OpEx stay fixed when hours drop. The accelerated ramp-up case does the opposite: SEK 33.18B net sales and SEK 3.00B EBIT (9.0%). Drag the sliders on Scenario Analysis to test your own mix.

q: What does this mean for S&OP and production planning?

r.narrative: Revenue here is recognised over time, so the finance forecast is only as good as the build plan behind it. The SEK 0.92B gap is a timing gap from the production side: Gripen E/F hours and acceptance milestones moving into 2027. The next step is to feed the S&OP build plan (airframe slots, hours by site, supplier delivery dates) straight into this forecast, so a slipped engine delivery shows up as a revenue and cash change the same day instead of at the next quarterly review. Q4 already carries SEK 9.0B, 31% of the year, so the December acceptance plan is the one to watch.

q: What does a 10-day production halt on Gripen E/F cost?

r.narrative: A 10-day stop on Gripen E/F final assembly in Linköping, with half of the lost hours recovered this year on overtime, costs SEK 141M of FY2026 EBIT, about SEK 14M per working day and 8.7% of the SEK 1,633M forecast EBIT. The biggest pieces are lost margin on revenue that slips into 2027 (SEK 42M) and idle labour (SEK 39M); SEK 206M of revenue moves into next year. Recovering 90% of the hours cuts the hit to SEK 77M, while a 20-day stop with no recovery costs SEK 443M. Open Production & Halt Cost to test other lines and durations.
